newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-RECORD DAY FOR VOELKER AND SJOBERG.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-RECORD DAY FOR VOELKER AND SJOBERG.

text.p: Olympic silver medallist Sandra Voelker bounced back from a surprise defeat to eclipse the European short-course record for the 100 metres freestyle on Friday.
The German had earlier been beaten into second place in the 50 metres butterfly by Sweden Johanna Sjoberg as both touched inside the previous European record time.
But Voelker's magnificent effort in the 100 freestyle was the outstanding swim of the first session of finals in the inaugural European sprints and short-course championships.
She was more than half a second clear at the halfway mark and swept on to touch in 53.04, a vast 1.42 seconds ahead of second-placed Susan Rolph of Britain.

The time emphatically beat the 53.33 European record set by German rival Franziska van Almsick in Beijing in January 1993 and was just 0.03 seconds outside the world mark of China's Le Jingyi, Olympic champion ahead of Voelker at the Atlanta Games in July.
"If it hadn't been for the 50 butterfly, which I swam barely half an hour before this race, I would have swum a world record today," Voelker said.
"On the last length I could feel the effects of the butterfly...I was still very satisfied with my 50 butterfly even though I lost. I was inside the old record after all."
Sjoberg just beat her in a thrilling duel in the 50 butterfly as both went under the European short-course mark set by Inge de Bruijn of the Netherlands in December 1991.
Sjoberg, 18, clocked 27.15 seconds and Voelker 27.23 to beat the 27.25 posted by de Bruijn at the 1991 European sprint championships in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.
Sjoberg and Voelker both earned 5,000 marks ($3,400) in prize money on offer for European records for the first time in a European championships.

"I didn't even notice that I'd set the first European record here. That's absolutely fantastic, particularly as there's prize money for the first time. I reckoned with a medal but not with gold," Sjoberg said.

Voelker, who collected a record 12 gold medals at the old European sprint championships held between 1991 and 1994, claimed her second title of the day when she anchored Germany to victory in the women's 4x50 freestyle relay.

Germany led the medals table after the first of three days of finals with five golds -- thanks to Voelker's 100 freestyle, the relay, Chris Bremer (men's 200 butterfly), Lars Conrad (men's 100 freestyle) and Sabine Herbst (women's 400 individual medley).
Sweden claimed a second gold after Sjoberg's triumph, Patrik Isaksson achieving an upset win in the men's 50 breaststroke when he pipped German Jens Kruppa by just 0.01 seconds in 27.76.
The Netherlands also finished the day in the Neptun pool with two golds, courtesy of Marcel Wouda in the men's 100 individual medley and Carla Geurts in the women's 800 freestyle.

Italy's Emiliano Brembilla, fourth in the 400 and 1,500 freestyle at this year's Atlanta Olympics, claimed the first of 38 titles at stake in these championships with a clearcut victory in the men's 400 freestyle.
